content:
maria: Heads up — noticed a canary rollout (c-472) that completed even though the caller (service account ops-runner) doesn't have deploy:canary. :eyes:

deploy-bot: canary c-472 started by ops-runner at 2026-03-19T14:20:30Z

ashok: Which pipeline triggered it? CI or ops manual?

maria: CI pipeline via the ad-hoc job. ops-runner should only have read perms. snippet from our RBAC: 
```
roles:
  - name: ops-runner
    perms: [deploy:read, metrics:read]
```

jules-security: Hmm. We shouldn't have allowed 'create-rollout' if deploy:canary missing. Could there be an impersonation or an authz bypass?

samir: I recall a hotfix months ago that added a temporary bypass for emergency rollouts. Could be left on. @erin-sre can you grep the rollout config for anything like bypass_perms?

erin-sre: grep returned one match in infra/rollout-config.yaml: 
```
canary:
  enabled: true
  bypass_perms: true   # emergency hotfix, intended temporary
```

maria: oh no. That flag should have been removed. Was the flag introduced with a feature-flag gate?

samir: It was introduced in a rush and gated behind feature flag rollout_authz_v2, but canary code path accidentally reads bypass_perms directly. We failed to centralize the authz call.

ashok: I pulled audit logs for ops-runner around the time: shows rollout.create -> 200, but I don't see an authz.check event for that request. log snippet: 
```
2026-03-19T14:20:30Z INFO rollout.create request_id=abc123 user=ops-runner status=200
# no authz.check recorded for request_id=abc123
```

jules-security: That matches a refactor regression: authz middleware moved to the shared router but the canary route used older handler that bypasses middleware when bypass_perms true. Looks like bypass_perms short-circuits authz entirely.

maria: Impact: non-admin service account can kick off canary rollouts — that's a privilege escalation vector for ops. We need immediate mitigation + followups.

samir: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) flip bypass_perms to false in prod (hotfix) 2) force-enable rollout_authz_v2 for canary route 3) add a temporary alert for any successful rollout where authz.check missing.

deploy-bot: canary c-472 finished successfully (duration 47s) :white_check_mark:

erin-sre: I deployed the flag flip to false in prod and restarted the rollout service. Verified canary path now hits authz middleware in staging.

ashok: I'm running a sweep to find other instances of bypass_perms:true across repos. found two other occurrences in partner integrations — adding PRs to remove.

jules-security: Followups (owners):
- @samir: open PR to remove bypass_perms handling and add unit + e2e test to assert authz runs for canary and rollout creation.
- @ashok: export audit logs for the last 72h and search for rollout.create without authz.check. Share findings in this thread.
- @maria: update incident runbook to include detection rule: if rollout created by non-admin and authz.check missing -> page oncall.

samir: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/987 (WIP) — adds tests + reverts bypass behavior.

maria: Also let's verify KMS/HSM usage: confirm ops-runner didn't get a new key or token that could explain impersonation. @ashok can you check KMS access logs?

ashok: KMS logs show no unusual key grants. ops-runner used existing service key; no rotations at the time.

jules-security: Good. Root cause = stale hotfix flag + refactor gap. No KMS compromise.

maria: Sounds good. If PR lands, let's schedule a small postmortem doc and add a regression to the CI gate.

samir: Will do. ETA for PR merge ~2hrs, rollout to prod ~4hrs after reviews.

jules-security: I'll create a short postmortem template and notify compliance. If anyone sees more suspicious rollouts, DM me immediately. :lock:

maria: Thanks all — nice triage.
